purpose: Sizing the candidate universe of apartment complexes for a Denver-metro rental data project

denver_residential_rental_licenses.notes: ENTITY_NAME is the license holder/owner (person or LLC), NOT a property/complex name. There is no unit-count field. LICENSE_TYPE is 100% uniform ('Residential Rental Property') and MULTIPLE_LICENSES is 100% 'Stand Alone' across all 38,553 records -- the dataset provides no field that flags a record as part of a multi-unit apartment complex. As a proxy, grouping by PARCEL_NUM shows 26,321 distinct parcels; 2,900 parcels have more than one license record, and 599 parcels have more than 4 license records (9,327 records total) -- these are candidate apartment-complex parcels, but this is an inferred proxy, not a dataset-provided classification.
denver_residential_rental_licenses.distinct_complex_names_note: Not determinable -- no complex/property name field exists in this dataset.

denver_assessor_apartment_parcels_option.query_used: where=PROP_CLASS='1225' (assessor property class code for apartments)
denver_assessor_apartment_parcels_option.note: Independently verified count (PROP_CLASS='1225', 1,759 parcels / 127,293 units) is in the same ballpark as, but does not exactly match, the reportedly-cited ~1,992 parcels / ~140,509 units -- likely due to a different class filter or a different data snapshot date. Not saved as a bulk JSON file (out of scope of the two required targets); figures were derived via ArcGIS REST outStatistics queries against the live service.
